words.tip: The general word for a place to live. 'Een woning zoeken' = to look for a home.
Belgian Dutch! In NL Dutch it's 'rijtjeshuis'. A house in a row, sharing both walls.
Belgian Dutch! Two houses joined as a pair (a 'house-pair'). NL: 'twee-onder-een-kap'.
French origin, stress on the last syllable.
'Op het platteland wonen' = to live in the countryside (use 'op', not 'in').
Short 'a'. Plural: de daken. 'op het dak' = on the roof.
Verwarmen = to heat. A selling point when house-hunting!
Openbaar = public. 'Met het openbaar vervoer' = by public transport.
'Aan de overkant' = across the street / on the other side.
Plural: de kamers. 'een huis met zeven kamers' = a house with seven rooms.
'eu' vowel. 'De keuken is vol licht' = the kitchen is full of light.
French origin — soft 'g' like the 's' in 'measure'. 'voor de garage' = in front of the garage.
'ui' vowel. 'Achter het huis is een tuin' = behind the house is a garden.
